transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-30
Time: 14:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Lee (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Morales (CTO, Midtown Clinic), Raj Singh (Head of Data), Lina Park (PM)

Summary: quick POC scoping focused on quality eval plan for the diagnostics summarization assistant. Customer cares about hallucination rate, format correctness for structured outputs, and latency at peak load. Agreed next steps and owners for benchmarks and data delivery.

Topics: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination checks, scoring approach, timelines, security notes (SOC2/KMS/VPC).

Action items (captured): see action_items metadata above.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros then jump into the quality eval plan.
[00:18] Dr. Morales: Hi, Elena here. We're excited but we have strict acceptance criteria.
[00:25] Raj: Raj, head of data. we'll provide sample EHR snippets, but need PHI scrubbed.
[00:31] Lina: Lina, product, I'll own acceptance criteria and user flows.
[00:38] Jonah: Jonah from Redwood infra/SE, I'll lead the benchmark and technical setup.
[00:42] Samira: Great, objective for today is agree on success criteria and the quality eval plan — golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination/format checks, and scoring approach. Also timeline for a 4-week POC.

[01:05] Dr. Morales: Our top success metric is clinical accuracy on discharge summary extraction — we need >= 92% exactness on key fields, and hallucination < 2% on critical items like medication lists.
[01:20] Raj: Also latency: we target p95 < 500ms for standard 512-token inference. Concurrency initially 20 req/s, peak 50 req/s. Cost is secondary but we want to compare hosted vs dedicated.

[02:00] Jonah: Ok for sizing that helps. For the benchmark we'll use 200 golden prompts representative of typical notes, plus 1,000 randomized evaluation items for statistical power. Golden prompts will be hand-labeled by your clinicians.
[02:20] Lina: We can deliver 50 labeled golden examples this week; need to know format.
[02:27] Samira: Format: JSON lines with fields: note_id, note_text, golden_outputs (structured fields), and an accept/reject flag. We'll send a template.

[03:10] Jonah: On the quality checks — we propose the following checks:
- Regression tests: run daily during POC against the golden set; diffs saved and regression score tracked.
- Hallucination checks: entity-level hallucination detection for meds, dosages, dates; report hallucination rate per field and per document.
- Format checks: validate JSON schema for structured outputs and count schema violations.
- Precision/Recall for extraction tasks and BLEU/ROUGE for free-text where applicable.

[04:05] Raj: How do you detect hallucination automatically? That's a big ask.
[04:12] Jonah: We use heuristic matching plus fuzzy string match and lookup against canonical lists (med list, ICD code tables). For ambiguous items we'll surface to human review. Expect some false positives in automated detection — that's why we include a manual adjudication step for a 200-sample subset.

[05:00] Samira: Scoring approach suggested:
- Field extraction: F1 per field, aggregated weighted score (clinical fields weighted higher).
- Hallucination: percentage of hallucinated critical fields (meds, allergies).
- Format: percentage of valid outputs.
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k requests.
- Overall pass/fail: must hit weighted quality >= 0.90 AND hallucination on critical fields < 2% AND p95 latency < 500ms.

[06:20] Dr. Morales: Weighted quality >= 0.90 seems reasonable. For some fields like allergy we may require near 98% recall.

[06:45] Jonah: For benchmarks we'll run model variants: base open model, quantized variant, and Redwood-verified low-latency variant. We'll capture tokens per request and cost estimate for each setup. Also include KV cache enabled runs to measure delta in latency for repeated prefixes.

[07:30] Raj: Onsecurity, social: we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS integration, and audit logs for inference. Also data residency: all PHI must remain in our VPC during POC.

[07:50] Samira: Yes we support Private deployment for VPC and KMS. For POC we can run a Private evaluation or a dedicated hosted instance with an isolated tenant. We'll send the security checklist and our SOC2 report.

[08:20] Lina: Timeline — customer prefers 4-week POC: week 0 onboarding, week 1 golden set + bench harness, week 2 full benchmark, week 3 review + iterate, week 4 decision. Feels aggressive but doable.

[08:40] Jonah: Agree. Proposed milestone dates: start 2027-01-10, initial benchmark by 2027-01-17, deliver report 2027-01-24, final review 2027-01-27. We'll include daily regression runs and a shared dashboard.

[09:15] Raj: Data transfer — we'll provide S3 exports with PHI stripped. For the internal tests we can do synthetic notes where needed.

[09:30] Samira: We'll provide a data template and an import script. Note: please confirm if you want Redwood to host the benchmark or run in your environment. Hosting with isolated tenant is fastest. Private deployment will need additional setup.

[10:00] Dr. Morales: We'd prefer isolated hosted for speed, but if KMS/VPC required we may need Private. We'll confirm with security team.

[10:25] Jonah: Technical benchmark details:
- Golden prompts: 200 hand-labeled prompts covering common and edge cases (medication lists, allergies, multi-lingual snippets).
- Regression test suite: each commit/variant auto-runs the golden set and 1k random items.
- Hallucination checks: exact match and fuzzy match against canonical vocab, and cross-field consistency checks (e.g., medication dose vs frequency).
- Format checks: strict JSON schema validator; count schema errors.
- Scoring: per-field F1, macro-averaged, then weighted aggregate. Also produce confusion matrices for key fields.

[12:05] Raj: Any planned human evaluation?
[12:10] Jonah: Yes — a 200-sample adjudication where clinicians mark false positives/negatives for hallucination samples. That will calibrate the automated detector. We'll also run pairwise A/B comparisons between model variants for subjective quality.

[12:40] Samira: About reporting: we'll provide a dashboard with time-series for regression score, hallucination rate, schema errors, latency, and estimated cost. We'll also export CSV and a short executive summary for your leadership.

[13:10] Lina: If we find regressions after a model change, what's the rollback plan?
[13:15] Jonah: We'll use Redwood rollouts with canary and automatic fallback to previous model if regression threshold exceeded. We'll include canary rules in the POC so you can simulate rollouts.

[13:45] Dr. Morales: One more question: how deterministic are the outputs? We need reproducible structured outputs for audit.
[13:52] Jonah: We can set sampling to deterministic (temperature 0) and pin model versions. For non-determinism we capture full generation logs and KV cache state; but recommend deterministic settings for structured extraction.

[14:20] Samira: Recap / next steps: Samira will send POC SOW and pricing, Jonah will share the benchmark harness and template for golden prompts, Raj will provide 50 labeled examples and S3 access, Lina to share acceptance criteria. We tentatively schedule POC start 2027-01-10.

[14:50] Dr. Morales: Sounds good. Appreciate the clarity on hallucination detection and the adjudication step.

[15:00] Samira: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the security docs and a calendar invite for kickoff.

[15:10] Meeting ends.
